reference: Polymetallic massive sulfide, Potter Mine (Commons title)

description.lithology: The visible core pieces are fine-grained, dark coloured, strongly foliated / laminated rocks. Top row left piece is very dark black to dark grey with a swirled / contorted laminated fabric; top row right piece is dark grey to black with a wavy, banded / foliated fabric with lighter grey laminae and minor yellow-green patches on the surface. Bottom row piece is a medium to dark grey-green rock with a strongly foliated / banded fabric; the groundmass is a mottled green-grey to silvery-grey with a fine-grained schistose texture and a sub-parallel banding that is locally disrupted by a darker blue-black to black discontinuous zone on the left side of the piece. The overall appearance is consistent with a fine-grained metasediment / metavolcanic schist / possibly banded iron formation / sulfide-bearing schist.
description.alteration: Alteration is visible as a pervasive to moderate greenish discolouration on the top right piece and especially on the bottom row piece, consistent with chloritic alteration with a green to yellow-green surface staining. No strong silicification, sericitization, potassic or carbonate alteration is clearly identifiable in the photo; oxidation is not clearly visible. Intensity is moderate to pervasive on the bottom piece, weak to moderate on the top right piece.
description.mineralization: No definitive sulfide mineral can be confidently identified at the photo resolution. The yellow-green patches on the top right piece and the green-grey mottling on the bottom piece are suggestive of secondary copper / iron alteration / possibly disseminated sulfides, but no clear pyrite, chalcopyrite, pyrrhotite, sphalerite or galena grains, blebs, veinlets or semi-massive to massive sulphide are unambiguously visible. Estimated volume percent cannot be reliably estimated from the image. Reported as none visible with certainty.

anomalies.explanation: The bottom row core piece shows a prominent dark blue-black to black irregular to sub-vertical zone on the left third of the piece that contrasts with the surrounding green-grey foliated groundmass; this could be a sulfide-rich band, a lithological contact or a vein and should be checked in hand specimen.

Core is presented in at least two tray rows; the top row contains two separate core pieces with a gap between them and the bottom row contains a single longer piece. The top left piece is broken / irregular on the right edge and the top right piece is broken / irregular on the bottom edge; broken or missing core geometry is visible but recovery cannot be estimated from the photo.
